title: Pullback of the quotient by an ideal
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, $f^*$ the pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback] and $\mathcal I=\mathcal J\mathcal O_X\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ the image of the composite $f^*\mathcal J\to f^*\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] (Stacks writes $f^{-1}\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal O_X$: the ideal sheaf generated by $f^\sharp(f^{-1}\mathcal J)$). Products $\mathcal K\mathcal F$ of a quasi-coherent ideal and a module, the powers $\mathcal K^n$ and the quotients $\mathcal F/\mathcal K\mathcal F$ are as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0). Then: (1) $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_X$, and for affine opens $V\subseteq Y$ and $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$, $\mathcal I(U)$ is the ideal of $\mathcal O_X(U)$ generated by the image of $\mathcal J(V)$ under $f^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y(V)\to\mathcal O_X(U)$; (2) for every $n\ge1$, $\mathcal J^n\mathcal O_X=\mathcal I^n$; (3) for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal G$ [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with quotient map $q_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G$, the morphism $f^*q_{\mathcal G}:f^*\mathcal G\to f^*(\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G)$ is an epimorphism with kernel $\mathcal I\cdot f^*\mathcal G$; hence, with $p_{\mathcal G}:f^*\mathcal G\to f^*\mathcal G/\mathcal I f^*\mathcal G$ the quotient map, there is a unique isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\sigma_{\mathcal G}:f^*\mathcal G/\mathcal I f^*\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*(\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G)$ with $\sigma_{\mathcal G}\circ p_{\mathcal G}=f^*q_{\mathcal G}$, and it is natural in $\mathcal G$: for every $\mathcal O_Y$-linear $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ between quasi-coherent modules, with induced maps $\bar u:\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'/\mathcal J\mathcal G'$ and $\overline{f^*u}:f^*\mathcal G/\mathcal If^*\mathcal G\to f^*\mathcal G'/\mathcal If^*\mathcal G'$, one has $\sigma_{\mathcal G'}\circ\overline{f^*u}=f^*(\bar u)\circ\sigma_{\mathcal G}$.

proof.text: (Notation and a basis.) For affine opens $V\subseteq Y$ and $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ put $A=\mathcal O_Y(V)$, $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $\rho=\rho_{V,U}:A\to B$, $\rho(a)=f^\sharp_V(a)|_U$; for an $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal H$, an open $W\subseteq Y$ and $s\in\mathcal H(W)$ write $f^*s=\eta_{\mathcal H}(s)\in(f^*\mathcal H)(f^{-1}W)$, $\eta$ the unit of $f^*\dashv f_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $\mathfrak B$ be the set of affine opens $U\subseteq X$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$ for some affine open $V\subseteq Y$. It is a basis of the topology of $X$: for $x\in W\subseteq X$ open choose an affine open $V\ni f(x)$ of $Y$ and then an affine open $U\ni x$ inside $W\cap f^{-1}(V)$ (affine opens form a basis of a scheme [def-pc-scheme]). Two facts about $\mathfrak B$ are used below. (a) Two sub-$\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal S,\mathcal S'$ of a sheaf $\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal S(U)=\mathcal S'(U)$ for all $U\in\mathfrak B$ are equal: for $s\in\mathcal S(W)$ cover $W$ by members $U_k$ of $\mathfrak B$; then $s|_{U_k}\in\mathcal S'(U_k)$, these agree on overlaps and glue in the sheaf $\mathcal S'$ to $t\in\mathcal S'(W)$ with $t|_{U_k}=s|_{U_k}$, so $t=s$ in $\mathcal F$; symmetrically. (b) A morphism of sheaves bijective on every member of $\mathfrak B$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis] (b). Finally $\mathcal O_X$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module: on an affine open $U$ with $B=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $\mathcal O_X|_U=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}B}$ and $\widetilde B$ both have the sections $B_r$ on $D(r)$, compatibly with restrictions [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], so they are isomorphic by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis] (applied to the basis of the $D(r)$) and $\mathcal O_X|_U\cong\widetilde B$ [pqf-def-coherent]; likewise for $\mathcal O_Y$.

proof.text: (Clause (1).) Let $\iota:\mathcal J\to\mathcal O_Y$ be the inclusion, $\epsilon:f^*\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_X$ the morphism adjoint to $f^\sharp$, characterized by $\epsilon(f^*a)=f^\sharp_W(a)$ for $a\in\mathcal O_Y(W)$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf], and $\varphi=\epsilon\circ f^*\iota:f^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal O_X$; by [def-nagata-extended-ideal] $\mathcal I=\operatorname{Im}\varphi$, the sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of local sections locally in the image of $\varphi$, which is contained in $\mathcal O_X$, i.e. a sheaf of ideals. $f^*\mathcal J$ is quasi-coherent because $\mathcal J$ is [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent], and $\mathcal O_X$ is quasi-coherent (step 1), so by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (2), (3) $\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent and $\mathcal I(U)=\varphi_U((f^*\mathcal J)(U))$ for every affine open $U$. Now let $V\subseteq Y$, $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ be affine opens. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] (surjectivity of $c_{\mathcal J}$) every element of $(f^*\mathcal J)(U)$ is a finite sum $\sum_kb_k(f^*s_k)|_U$ with $s_k\in\mathcal J(V)$, $b_k\in B$. For $s\in\mathcal J(V)$, naturality of the unit gives $(f^*\iota)(f^*s)=f^*(\iota(s))$, hence $\varphi(f^*s)=\epsilon(f^*s)=f^\sharp_V(s)$ in $\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}V)$, and as $\varphi$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear and commutes with restriction, $\varphi_U(\sum_kb_k(f^*s_k)|_U)=\sum_kb_k\rho(s_k)$. Therefore $\mathcal I(U)=\{\sum_kb_k\rho(s_k)\}=\rho(\mathcal J(V))B$, the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of $\mathcal J(V)$ under $f^\sharp$. This is (1).

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01IC (lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent) and Lemma 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback); Modules, Lemma 01BG (lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent), modules.tex

proof.text: (Clause (2).) Fix $n\ge1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (1), (2) on $Y$, $\mathcal J^n$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals with $\mathcal J^n(V)=\mathcal J(V)^n$ for affine $V$; so step 2 applies to $\mathcal J^n$: $\mathcal J^n\mathcal O_X$ is a quasi-coherent ideal with $(\mathcal J^n\mathcal O_X)(U)=\rho(\mathcal J(V)^n)B$ for $U\in\mathfrak B$ over $V$. By step 2, $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent ideal of $\mathcal O_X$, so by the same node on $X$, $\mathcal I^n$ is a quasi-coherent ideal with $\mathcal I^n(U)=\mathcal I(U)^n=(\rho(\mathcal J(V))B)^n$. For a ring map $\rho:A\to B$ and an ideal $\mathfrak a\subseteq A$, $(\rho(\mathfrak a)B)^n=\rho(\mathfrak a^n)B$: $(\rho(\mathfrak a)B)^n$ is generated by the products $\rho(a_1)\cdots\rho(a_n)=\rho(a_1\cdots a_n)$, $a_i\in\mathfrak a$, and $\mathfrak a^n$ is additively generated by the $a_1\cdots a_n$, so both ideals have the same generators. Hence $(\mathcal J^n\mathcal O_X)(U)=\mathcal I^n(U)$ for all $U\in\mathfrak B$, and the two sub-$\mathcal O_X$-modules of $\mathcal O_X$ are equal by step 1 (a): $\mathcal J^n\mathcal O_X=\mathcal I^n$.

proof.text: (Clause (3) on affine opens.) Let $\mathcal G$ be quasi-coherent, $q=q_{\mathcal G}$, and put $\mathcal K=\mathcal I\cdot f^*\mathcal G$ with quotient map $p=p_{\mathcal G}:f^*\mathcal G\to f^*\mathcal G/\mathcal K$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0). By [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (1), (2) on $Y$, $\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent and, for affine $V$ with $\mathfrak a=\mathcal J(V)$, $M=\mathcal G(V)$, $q_V:M\to(\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G)(V)$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak aM$. $f^*\mathcal G$ and $f^*(\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G)$ are quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent], and $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent ideal (step 2), so by the same node on $X$, $\mathcal K$ is quasi-coherent and for $U\in\mathfrak B$ over $V$: $\mathcal K(U)=\mathcal I(U)(f^*\mathcal G)(U)=\rho(\mathfrak a)B\cdot(f^*\mathcal G)(U)$ (step 2) and $p_U$ is surjective with kernel $\mathcal K(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] there are $B$-linear isomorphisms $c_{\mathcal G}:M\otimes_AB\to(f^*\mathcal G)(U)$ and $c_{\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G}:(\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G)(V)\otimes_AB\to(f^*(\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G))(U)$ with $(f^*q)_U\circ c_{\mathcal G}=c_{\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G}\circ(q_V\otimes1_B)$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] to the exact sequence $\mathfrak aM\to M\xrightarrow{q_V}(\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G)(V)\to0$ and $B$: $q_V\otimes1$ is surjective and its kernel is the image of $\mathfrak aM\otimes_AB$, the subgroup generated by the elements $am\otimes b=\rho(a)\cdot(m\otimes b)$ ($a\in\mathfrak a$, $m\in M$, $b\in B$), which is the $B$-submodule $\rho(\mathfrak a)B\cdot(M\otimes_AB)$. Transporting along the $B$-linear isomorphisms $c$: $(f^*q)_U$ is surjective with kernel $c_{\mathcal G}(\rho(\mathfrak a)B\cdot(M\otimes_AB))=\rho(\mathfrak a)B\cdot(f^*\mathcal G)(U)=\mathcal K(U)$, for every $U\in\mathfrak B$.

(Clause (3): $\sigma_{\mathcal G}$, epimorphism, kernel.) The sectionwise kernel $\ker(f^*q)$ is a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of $f^*\mathcal G$ with $\ker(f^*q)(U)=\mathcal K(U)$ for all $U\in\mathfrak B$ (step 4), so $\ker(f^*q)=\mathcal K$ by step 1 (a); in particular $f^*q$ vanishes on $\mathcal K$. As $p$ is the cokernel of the inclusion $\mathcal K\to f^*\mathcal G$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0), there is a unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\sigma_{\mathcal G}:f^*\mathcal G/\mathcal K\to f^*(\mathcal G/\mathcal J\mathcal G)$ with $\sigma_{\mathcal G}\circ p=f^*q$; uniqueness also follows from $p$ being an epimorphism [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (1). For $U\in\mathfrak B$, $p_U$ and $(f^*q)_U$ are both surjective with kernel $\mathcal K(U)$ (step 4), so $\sigma_{\mathcal G,U}$ is bijective; by step 1 (b), $\sigma_{\mathcal G}$ is an isomorphism. Hence $f^*q=\sigma_{\mathcal G}\circ p$ is an epimorphism (composite of an epimorphism and an isomorphism), with kernel $\mathcal K=\mathcal I\cdot f^*\mathcal G$.

proof.text: (Naturality.) Let $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ be $\mathcal O_Y$-linear between quasi-coherent modules. Since $u$ commutes with the multiplication maps ($u\circ m_{\mathcal G}=m_{\mathcal G'}\circ(1_{\mathcal J}\otimes u)$ for $m:\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$), it maps $\mathcal J\mathcal G$ into $\mathcal J\mathcal G'$ and induces a unique $\bar u$ with $\bar u\circ q_{\mathcal G}=q_{\mathcal G'}\circ u$; likewise $f^*u$ maps $\mathcal If^*\mathcal G$ into $\mathcal If^*\mathcal G'$ and induces $\overline{f^*u}$ with $\overline{f^*u}\circ p_{\mathcal G}=p_{\mathcal G'}\circ f^*u$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0). By functoriality of $f^*$ [def-pc-module-pullback] and step 5: $\sigma_{\mathcal G'}\circ\overline{f^*u}\circ p_{\mathcal G}=\sigma_{\mathcal G'}\circ p_{\mathcal G'}\circ f^*u=f^*q_{\mathcal G'}\circ f^*u=f^*(q_{\mathcal G'}\circ u)=f^*(\bar u\circ q_{\mathcal G})=f^*\bar u\circ f^*q_{\mathcal G}=f^*\bar u\circ\sigma_{\mathcal G}\circ p_{\mathcal G}$, and $p_{\mathcal G}$ is an epimorphism, so $\sigma_{\mathcal G'}\circ\overline{f^*u}=f^*(\bar u)\circ\sigma_{\mathcal G}$.
